findings.summary: The plan does not say how the coverage test decides which section or R a requirement belongs to.
findings.evidence: The Olympus headings in BRIEF.md (read, lines 560–856) include subsections such as '### 3.1 Preserve the original signal', '### Stage A — Understand and reproduce', '### Loop A — Deliver outcomes' and '### R1 — Causal investigation'. Section 3 can be covered only through 3.1–3.3, and section 4 only through its stages. The plan names a coverage test but gives no rule that maps a source heading to its parent section. Fix: State the rule. For example, a source heading counts toward the nearest enclosing '## N.' heading in the split, and toward 'R<n>' when it equals the '### R<n> — …' heading. Build that mapping from the splitter's heading hierarchy, not from string prefixes.
findings.location: Plan: Steps 3–4 and the coverage test; Demonstration for criterion 5

findings.summary: The claim that serde enums reject an out-of-range kind or status has no test that exercises it.
findings.evidence: The demonstration says 'serde enums reject any kind outside goal/requirement/constraint/acceptance and any status outside active/superseded', but Step 4 lists no parse-failure test. As written, it only shows that the types exist. Fix: Add a small in-memory parse test: a TOML requirement with kind = "wish", and one with status = "draft", must both fail to deserialize. Optionally add one with a missing statement.

findings.summary: Some section bodies are short and need care.
findings.evidence: '## 6. Requirements for systemic learning' (line 784) is followed directly by '### R1' (line 786). Under the strict next-heading rule its body is a single line, so quotes for section 6 itself have little room and almost all must cite R headings. The design handles this correctly; it is noted only so the producer is not surprised. Fix: No change needed. The producer should cite R headings for R content.

summary: I read BRIEF.md, xtask/Cargo.toml, xtask/tests/policy.rs, docs/enforcement.md and docs/decisions.md in the snapshot. The plan matches the request and the accepted reading, and its claims hold up against those files. The Olympus headings in the plan's range (lines 550 to 864) are unique, so heading-scoped matching works. toml and serde are already dev-dependencies of xtask, so no Cargo change is needed. The next free ids really are M33 and D114 (M32 and D113 are the last ones in use). M24 (every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists) requires the test names in the M33 row to be real functions, and the plan accounts for that. I checked the M19 boundary words against lines 550 to 864: the only hit is the Hermes row at line 597, which the plan already handles by quoting only the part before the word. Each behavior criterion has a negative test that would fail without the behavior: bad quote, duplicate id, dangling supersedes, missing source, missing coverage, wrong heading, and a subsection quote cited under its parent heading. The work fits one producer run. Remaining findings are minor: how coverage maps subsection headings to sections 1 to 5 and to R1 to R8 is unstated, and the enum rejection of a bad kind or status has no test.
